note: Adapted from the original description by Schmitz (1917), written in German; covers the soldier and the worker; the alate is undescribed (the original states that only soldiers and workers are known). Type locality: the upper Congo River near Stanleyville.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Similar to the soldier of Microcerotermes parvus in size and colour, distinguished by stronger mandibular teeth, a distinctly notched anterior margin of the pronotum, and a fontanelle. The fontanelle resembles that of Microcerotermes libericus. Measurements: body length (including mandibles) 4.5 mm, head with mandibles 2.1 mm, head without mandibles 1.4 mm, head width 0.8 mm, mandibles (including base) 0.94 mm. Head yellow, reddish yellow in front; mandibles brownish black with a yellow-red base; antennal segments pale yellow with white bases; legs and the margin of the pronotum yellowish white, abdomen whitish. Head elongate, sides parallel, posterior corners rounded; frons slightly raised forward from the fontanelle region, then evenly and gently sloping forward; fontanelle at the end of the anterior third of the frons, a pale spot without a raised rim. Labrum wider than long, pentagonal, the angles rounded. Mandibles robust, straight in lateral view, outer margin strongly curved in dorsal view; the teeth of the inner margin stronger than in most species, almost always one conspicuous large tooth on the proximal half, sometimes bidentate. Antennae 13-segmented, the last two segments extending beyond the mandibles; segment 2 half as long as segment 1 and about as long as segments 3 and 4 together; segment 3 very short but not distinctly narrower than the segment behind it. Anterior lobe of the pronotum narrow and short, with a distinct median notch. Legs sparsely setose; middle tibia with 2 shorter, strong subapical spines on the outer side besides the apical spur; hind tibia 0.67 mm long.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Larger individuals 3.5 mm long, smaller ones 3 mm; head pale yellow, darker in front, the reddish grey gut contents showing through the abdomen; antennae 13-segmented; hind tibia 0.6 mm long.
